A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LCEN research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, allowing relocated material to be matched and substantive revisions to be compared.

before.justification: v1 reports original LCEN experiments on synthetic data, physical-law recovery and empirical prediction benchmarks, alongside some reproduced results from earlier work.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds housing prediction, electricity-load forecasting and component ablations, including results in Appendices A4 and A6.

M1.justification: The feature expansion and LASSO–Clip–EN–Clip procedure remain unchanged. v2 explicitly specifies scaled inputs and absolute-value clipping, consistent with v1's scaled-coefficient description and retained negative coefficients. The new ablated architectures are experimental comparisons, not replacements for LCEN.

E1.justification: v2 adds modified Boston housing price prediction and consumption-only GEFCom 2014 electricity forecasting, including multiple forecast horizons. It removes the Newton's Law of Cooling experiment. CARMENES and both Kepler datasets remain, with their detailed results moved to Appendix A6.1.

E2.justification: Diesel and abalone comparisons gain RF, GBDT, AdaB, SVM, MLP, MLP-GL1 and LassoNet; abalone additionally gains PLS. Concrete gains six nonlinear comparators while retaining Yeh's ANN under the name MLP. The new forecasting comparison includes published TCN, RNN, LSTM, GRU and Seq2Seq results.

E3.justification: New protocols include Boston's 20% test split and B-variable preprocessing, plus GEFCom training on task 1, testing on tasks 2–15, lag 168 and forecasts spanning 24–168 hours. Table 1 changes coefficient-error reporting from MSE to RMSE, and concrete R2 reporting is removed. Existing diesel, abalone and concrete split descriptions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A4 newly compares five ablated or variant pipelines across relativistic energy, diesel, abalone and concrete. These experiments test the contributions of clipping and the choice/order of LASSO and EN through accuracy, selection and runtime measurements. Table 6 additionally examines forecasting performance over longer horizons.

E5.justification: v1 reports median polynomial test MSEs; v2 additionally reports their 25th and 75th percentiles in Figure A2. This adds dispersion reporting for an existing experiment. Neither version explicitly documents run counts or seeds, so the changed degree-selection frequency scale does not establish a particular increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 revise high-noise coefficients and report correct feature sets where v1 reported spurious features. The reported diesel LCEN model changes from 4.86°C RMSE with 37 features to 4.83°C with 36; concrete test RMSE changes from 5.82 to 5.73 MPa. Abalone counts and sparse-model results, polynomial median curves and degree-selection frequencies also change. New benchmarks, ablations and quartiles add substantial results. These are revised reports, not established identical-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Removing the cooling experiment also removes its finite-difference derivation from Newton's differential equation and associated heat-transfer parameter reasoning in v1 Section 3.2. The retained physical-law equations and feature expansion are unchanged; no new LCEN theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v1's abstract claims comparability to an ANN on one dataset. v2 broadens this to comparable or better performance against ANNs on multiple datasets and explicitly includes sparse nonlinear competitors. Its introduction adds a faster-than-most-architectures claim, while the discussion adds superiority over Seq2Seq forecasting and applicability to nonscientific problems.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of the component ablations and accuracy–sparsity–runtime tradeoffs against stronger competitors. It explicitly limits LCEN to functions in its feature expansion, states that it is not a universal approximator, and acknowledges circumstances favoring dense deep learning. The cooling-specific physical interpretation is removed.

D1.justification: New Appendix A3 documents regularization grids, cutoff ranges, neural-network sizes, training budgets and scheduling details. Appendix A7 specifies CPU, RAM and GPU resources. New dataset preprocessing and access information are also supplied. These substantially expand v1's limited implementation documentation without establishing that previously reported experiments used different settings.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially expands coverage of nonlinear feature selection, group-sparse neural networks, LassoNet, concrete autoencoders, stochastic gates and shortcut learning. LCEN is positioned against these methods through interpretability and computational tradeoffs. Forecasting and hybrid-model literature is added, while cooling-related sources are removed.

P1.justification: The introduction and discussion are substantially expanded and rewritten around nonlinear competitors, broader applications and limitations. Algorithm 1 and detailed physical-law results move to appendices, empirical results are reorganized, and dedicated hyperparameter, ablation and computational-resource appendices are introduced. The separate Impact Statement is removed.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two columns to one. Comparison tables are expanded, forecasting and ablation tables and a quartile figure are added, and Table 2's subtables become side by side. The algorithm, abalone table, physical-law summary and multicollinearity figure are relocated; polynomial plots are redrawn, including a changed degree-frequency scale.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in v1 through component ablations, broader nonlinear and sparse-neural comparisons, and substantial reproducibility documentation in Appendices A3–A4 and A7. Quartile reporting and explicit applicability limits further strengthen assessment of the method. These gains outweigh losing the cooling case, although reporting inconsistencies remain: Appendix A4 calls LCEN most accurate on diesel despite ENC's 4.80°C RMSE versus LCEN's 4.83°C in the corresponding tables.
